1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would always be free for open source. Plenty of people told us we were crazy. How would we make money, they asked.

Today we run on 1,200 repositories, and about 900 of them are open source.

Here is what really surprised me.

Across all those repos, 1 in 7 CI failures turned out to be a flaky test. One in seven. That adds up to countless hours of developer time wasted on red builds that were not real failures.

Open source gave us more than users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers, and we shipped it on November 12.

Giving back is not charity. It is strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

That was when it hit us. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding another one.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025, we made a tough call and moved everything into WhatsApp.

The results speak for themselves: 140 outlets, and a median reply time to shift messages of under 20 minutes.

The lesson? Meet your users where they already are. Don't make them come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

Hardware is hard. Here's our story.

Our first production run at Shelfwise didn't go as planned. 400 labels shipped with a faulty battery contact.

We decided to recall and replace every one of those 400 labels, at our own cost. It set us back about $7,000. Painful? Absolutely. Worth it? 100%.

Because trust is everything.

We didn't stop there. We introduced a 100% contact test at the factory. Since then, we've had zero contact failures across 6,000 labels.

Mistakes don't define you. How you respond to them does.

To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.
